role: Root product design for the one authorized Source5 attempt. This is not an implementation, not QA, and not adoption of the rejected replacement options.
review_result: final_verdict.approved is false. Issues 129-R2-NONE, 129-R2-LEASE, 129-R2-SEAL, and 129-R2-RELEASE are non-empty. Unsupported claims 129-R2-U1, 129-R2-U2, and 129-R2-U3 are non-empty. The three report options are not approved. The decisions in that verdict are accepted, and 129-R2-NONE allows this later design under the recorded operator authority.

ancestry.reason: Source3 passed the eleven Generator commands and remains rejected for 129-B1 and 129-B2. Source5 repairs those two defects on that product ancestry. It does not copy Source3 into the handover checkout as adopted product and does not revive the disproved monitor.

lisp_rule: Leave tools/sbcl_session_loop.lisp byte-identical to a9114bcbe16fba76dbdba1147ea76db8a5a6b39d unless a Python transport change makes that impossible. If a Lisp change is required, stop and report it. Do not invent one.

capture.primitive: For each gating input, read the path once with a single read of all bytes into a private buffer. Parse and hash only that buffer. Do not hash a later read, and do not decide attempt_ok from an earlier read than the hashed bytes.
forbidden_mechanisms: F_SETLEASE and every read-lease exclusion or currentness claim
inotify, fanotify, directory watches, inode watches, mtime, and ctime
treating a sealed memfd or other copied buffer as the authoritative run_state or original path
capture.seals: Not used. Probe evidence shows seals can freeze a copy. They are not original-path authority, and this design does not need them.

actions.poll-operation: No helper job. Return the observed durable snapshot, as contract 127 already requires.
actions.cancel-operation: No helper job and no read of operations/*.json. On the supervisor, publish cancel_requested and cancellation_confirmed false for the current outstanding operation, then send one correlated cancel frame. Latency must not grow with history size.
actions.close-session: No helper job and no read of operations/*.json. Use the existing bounded close: no project code, reap the owned runtime group, preserve records, and return infrastructure/70 when death is uncertain. Do not report that uncertainty as cancellation or success.
actions.open-session: Helper reads the governed run_state once and binds the attempt from those bytes.
actions.submit-operation: Supervisor still checks duplicate operation ids before the helper. The helper reads the governed run_state once. Crash-disagreement reconciliation may read retained operation and result files inside the helper and must not put those files in the response.
actions.reattach-session: Helper reads the governed run_state once and reads each declared manifest file once. Git HEAD and template checks use the outputs captured in that same job. The certificate binds those captured bytes.
actions.transfer-session: Same helper shape as open for the governed attempt and live identity. No history table in the response.

certificate.prohibited: No files array, no per-path stamp, and no per-path SHA row.
certificate.input_digest: sha256 over the gating buffers in a documented stable order. The attempt value in the certificate is the integer parsed from the same run_state buffer that entered the digest.
certificate.frame: The encoded job result must fit in the existing FRAME_LIMIT of 65536 bytes. Oversize remains infrastructure failure. Cancel and close never produce this result, so history growth cannot block them through this frame.

pre_apply_recheck.where: Immediately before apply_request, on the supervisor, for open, submit, reattach, and transfer.
pre_apply_recheck.check_live: A present certificate must not make check_live return immediately.
pre_apply_recheck.verified_attempt: Do not apply a cached attempt_ok. Re-read run_state from disk. Refuse unless its attempts integer equals both certificate attempt_value and request.attempt, and the session contract_id and step_key still match.
pre_apply_recheck.inputs: Re-read every gating path in the same order, recompute input_digest, and refuse unless it equals the certificate. A changed file fails closed before execution.
pre_apply_recheck.version: Refuse unless the supervisor version still equals the version captured when the job started. An external edit that does not change the supervisor version is caught by the digest recheck, not by the version alone.

deadlines.cancellation_confirmation: Unchanged. It confirms runtime unwind or terminates the proven owned runtime group. It is not a budget for history I/O.
deadlines.why_30: Contract 127 already bounds an explicit timed poll at 30 seconds. This separate helper budget uses that existing ceiling.
deadlines.on_expiry: Infrastructure failure, stop only the proven owned helper group, do not apply the certificate, and do not report cancellation or successful completion.
